subject: sociology
title: Mass Media Meets New Media
welcome_lead: From printing presses to TikTok feeds, see how the media has reshaped sociology's questions about power and influence.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on mass and new media, ownership, audience and basic media effects.
final_note: You can now distinguish mass from new media and name the main effects models.

concepts.def: Channels reaching huge audiences: TV, papers, radio.
Interactive digital media like apps and social sites.
The people who receive media messages.
Idea media inject ideas directly into a passive audience.
Audiences actively pick media for their own needs.
Different media merging onto one device, e.g. a phone.

walkthroughs.body_html: Mass media (TV news, newspapers) is one-to-many and passive. New media (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) is many-to-many: audiences can create, share and reply, blurring the line between producer and consumer.
The hypodermic syringe model claims media inject powerful messages directly into passive viewers, who then act on them. Often used to argue that violent media cause violent behaviour.
Blumler and Katz argued audiences are active: they choose media for entertainment, information, identity and social interaction. The same show can mean different things to different viewers.

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.
Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
School subjects must match employer demands.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
